packages.name: Heavy Push
packages.summary: Run behind extra blockers for a few yards.
packages.inspiration: Gridiron short yardage: extra blockers, downhill runs.
packages.scenario: Four or fewer yards to go.
packages.benefits: A team from any book can lean on its biggest bodies to move the chains.
packages.cost: Defenses see it coming, and it almost never breaks a long run.
packages.counter: A stacked box (Fortress) or extra rushers (Blitz Pack).

packages.name: Goal Line Jumbo
packages.summary: Pack the line and run into the end zone.
packages.inspiration: Gridiron jumbo package at the goal line.
packages.scenario: Inside the opponent's 12.
packages.benefits: Punches in a touchdown instead of settling for a kick.
packages.cost: A stuffed run burns a down with the kick still on the table.
packages.counter: Fortress, or Swarm rallying to the ball.

packages.name: Four Minute Grind
packages.summary: Use inside runs and short kick passes to protect a lead.
packages.inspiration: Gridiron four minute offense: run the ball and the clock with a lead.
packages.scenario: Leading in the fourth quarter.
packages.benefits: Keeps the ball out of the trailing team's hands.
packages.cost: Gives up big gains for safe ones; a quick stop hands the ball back with time left.

packages.name: Launch Pad Kick Set
packages.summary: Use short kick passes to reach snap kick range.
packages.inspiration: AFL forward 50 entries: work the ball into the scoring zone with straight kicks.
packages.scenario: Between the opponent's 45 and 15, or past midfield on downs 4 to 6.
packages.benefits: Short safe kick passes that set up a snap kick.
packages.cost: Without Boot Raid's kicking system the setup gains less: borrowed Boot Raid calls on the Launch Pad averaged 3.84 yards against 4.27 for home calls in the PR #329 prototype.

packages.name: Vertical Shot
packages.summary: Send a long kick pass downfield.
packages.inspiration: AFL contested marks: a long kick into traffic for a strong lead.
packages.scenario: Long yardage (5 or more yards a down needed), or chasing the game.
packages.benefits: Flips the field in one play.
packages.cost: The long release invites sacks, and a pick gives up a bonus possession.
packages.counter: Lockdown, Predator jumping routes, or Drift sitting deep.

packages.name: Quick Kick Chain
packages.summary: Gain manageable chunks with quick kick passes.
packages.inspiration: Gridiron West Coast offense; AFL short kicking to leading players.
packages.scenario: Long yardage: 5 or more yards a down needed, such as 3rd and 20.
packages.benefits: Chips back into a manageable distance without a deep shot. Borrowed long yardage calls gained 5.35 yards against 4.94 for home calls in the PR #329 prototype.
packages.cost: East Coast's rhythm meter does not travel, so a borrowed chain is only the plays.
packages.counter: Lockdown, or Drift giving up the short kick and tackling.

packages.name: Two Minute Chain
packages.summary: Move toward scoring range with quick kicks and laterals.
packages.inspiration: Gridiron two minute drill.
packages.scenario: Last two minutes of a half.
packages.benefits: Quick completions toward kicking range.
packages.cost: Small chunks against a soft zone.

packages.name: Chase Chain
packages.summary: Chase a deficit with laterals and kick passes.
packages.inspiration: Rugby sevens: keep the ball alive through hands.
packages.scenario: Trailing late.
packages.benefits: Big play chances when a team needs points.
packages.cost: Every lateral is a fumble chance and a bell for the other side.

packages.name: Kick-In Breakout
packages.summary: Kick to a teammate to escape deep field position.
packages.inspiration: AFL kick-ins: a planned first kick to a leading target out of the defensive goal square.
packages.scenario: First snap of a drive that starts inside the offense's own 10.
packages.benefits: A scripted way out of a deep start, which Delta Yards makes common for a leading team.
packages.cost: A pick that deep is a short field for the other side.
packages.counter: Predator, or a high press on the kick-in.

packages.name: Restart Go-To
packages.summary: Open the drive with a jet or sweep.
packages.inspiration: AFL center bounce set plays: the go-to players know where the first ball is going.
packages.scenario: First snap after the restart that follows the other team's score.
packages.benefits: Gets the ball to the best athlete before the defense settles.
packages.cost: Once scouted, the defense knows the first call.

packages.name: First Phase Strike
packages.summary: Open the drive with a misdirection run.
packages.inspiration: Rugby lineout and scrum strike moves: a planned first phase that bunches the defense and goes around it.
packages.scenario: First snap of a drive.
packages.benefits: A designed misdirection before the defense has read anything.
packages.cost: It is only a script: once the drive starts, the team plays its home book.
packages.counter: Chaos stunts blow up the script.

packages.name: Last Tackle Kick
packages.summary: Send a kick pass deep on a late down.
packages.inspiration: Rugby league's attacking kick on the last tackle of a set of six.
packages.scenario: Downs 4 to 6 between the opponent's 45 and 15.
packages.benefits: A planned kick into the scoring zone at the end of a set.
packages.cost: If it fails on sixth down, the ball turns over at the spot.
packages.counter: Lockdown or Drift keeping the deep field covered.

packages.name: Fast Break
packages.summary: Attack quickly on the first snap after a takeaway.
packages.inspiration: Lacrosse transition: push before the defense recovers from a turnover.
packages.scenario: First snap of a drive that started from a turnover or a bonus possession.
packages.benefits: Attacks a defense still sorting out its changes.
packages.cost: A quick miss puts its own defense back on the field.

packages.name: Extra Attacker
packages.summary: Run wide against a tired defense.
packages.inspiration: Lacrosse extra man offense: attack while the other side is short of fresh players.
packages.scenario: Defenders on the field average under 75 energy.
packages.benefits: Runs at tired legs, which is what Stampede's plays are built for.
packages.cost: Needs its own players fresh to win the race.
packages.counter: A defense that rotates in fresh players and rallies (Swarm).

packages.name: Viper Trail
packages.summary: Catch a short kick and use a trailing runner if crowded.
packages.inspiration: Gaelic football support running after a kick pass.
packages.scenario: Downs 1 to 4 between your own 20 and the opponent's 20.
packages.benefits: The receiver can keep the ball or feed a fresher runner behind them.
packages.cost: The extra exchange can be intercepted or dropped.
packages.counter: Follow the support runner and close the lateral lane.

packages.name: Far Side Coil
packages.summary: Work one edge with short kicks, then switch across the field.
packages.inspiration: Australian rules boundary play and switching the point of attack.
packages.scenario: Use during a drive with room on either side. The switch follows two setups and observed pressure.
packages.benefits: Uses short kicks to move the defense before testing the far side.
packages.cost: The cross field kick takes longer and the setup can use several downs.
packages.counter: Keep coverage wide so the far side stays protected.

packages.name: Third Strike
packages.summary: Draw pressure with repeat carries, then sweep the other edge.
packages.inspiration: Rugby phase play and sevens compression before expansion.
packages.scenario: Use on downs 1 to 4. Release to the opposite edge when the defense presses after two setups.
packages.benefits: The same look can threaten both edges over a series.
packages.cost: The setup can stall against a strong front.
packages.counter: Keep edge support in place while defending the carries.

packages.name: Bonus Guard
packages.summary: Use inside carries and short outlets while a bonus is pending.
packages.inspiration: Viperball's bonus possession creates a two drive scoring opportunity.
packages.scenario: Downs 1 to 4 after earning an interception bonus, outside the opponent’s 28.
packages.benefits: Uses inside runs in ordinary situations and a short kick pass when there is ground to make up on second or third down.
packages.cost: A defense waiting inside can stall the first drive.
packages.counter: Stack the box and make the offense spend its downs.

packages.name: Pindown Chase
packages.summary: Aim a late punt toward the end zone with a designated chaser.
packages.inspiration: Canadian football singles and rugby kick chase.
packages.scenario: On sixth down near midfield when tied or leading by at most five points and a scoring kick has low expected value.
packages.benefits: A directional punt and an available coverage player can earn a pindown.
packages.cost: Inaccurate placement can hand the return team better field position.
packages.counter: Field the kick cleanly and beat the first coverage player.

packages.name: Goal Line Stand
packages.summary: Stack the middle to stop runs near the goal line.
packages.inspiration: Gridiron goal line defense.
packages.scenario: The offense inside the defense's 12, or 4 or fewer to go.
packages.benefits: Takes away the inside run.
packages.cost: Leaves the edges and the short kick pass open.
packages.counter: Quick kick passes over a loaded box.

packages.name: Short Yardage Wall
packages.summary: Crowd the middle to deny short inside gains.
packages.inspiration: Gridiron short yardage front.
packages.scenario: Four or fewer to go.
packages.benefits: Fortress is rated strongest in short yardage (0.70).
packages.cost: Edges open. In the PR #329 runs, schemes rated strong in short yardage did not hold short yardage gains below other schemes, so the rating may not reach the yardage roll (flagged for the work queue).
packages.counter: Misdirection or laterals to the edge.

packages.name: Kick Range Shell
packages.summary: Drop into coverage to defend deeper kick passes.
packages.inspiration: AFL defensive 50 structure: protect the space in front of goal.
packages.scenario: The offense past midfield on downs 4 to 6, or on the Launch Pad.
packages.benefits: Lockdown suppresses kicks (kick_suppression 0.80) and denies the setup kick pass.
packages.cost: A lighter box gives up runs.

packages.name: Long Yardage Bracket
packages.summary: Spread the defense to take away long kick passes.
packages.inspiration: Gridiron long yardage coverage.
packages.scenario: Long yardage: 5 or more yards a down needed.
packages.benefits: Rated strong in long yardage (0.85).
packages.cost: Opens running lanes.

packages.name: Prevent
packages.summary: Protect deep space and concede short gains.
packages.inspiration: Gridiron prevent defense.
packages.scenario: Last two minutes of a half, or protecting a lead.
packages.benefits: Drift has the strongest explosive play suppression (0.55).
packages.cost: Gives up short gains that add up.

packages.name: Short Yardage Pressure
packages.summary: Send extra rushers to disrupt short runs.
packages.inspiration: Gridiron run blitz.
packages.scenario: Four or fewer to go.
packages.benefits: Blitz Pack is rated strong in short yardage (0.80).
packages.cost: DEF-06 measured about one more 30 yard play a game against Blitz Pack.
packages.counter: Counters and draws into the vacated gaps.

packages.name: Kick-In Press
packages.summary: Pressure an offense trying to kick out from deep.
packages.inspiration: AFL zone press on the kick-in: squeeze the short options and force a long kick.
packages.scenario: The offense's first snap inside its own 10.
packages.benefits: Jumps the short kick out of a deep start, where a pick is a short field.
packages.cost: Leaves space behind the press.
packages.counter: A planned breakout or a long kick over the top.

packages.name: Ride
packages.summary: Press the new offense after a change of possession.
packages.inspiration: Lacrosse ride: contest the clear right after losing the ball.
packages.scenario: The first snap after the other team took the ball away.
packages.benefits: Pressure before the new offense is organized.
packages.cost: Riding while changing lines risks getting caught short and giving up a fast break.
packages.counter: A fast break that beats the ride.

packages.name: Rush Line
packages.summary: Rush wide to cut off sweeps and laterals.
packages.inspiration: Rugby rush defense: line speed to shut down width.
packages.scenario: First or second down with 15 or more to go.
packages.benefits: Squeezes sweeps and lateral chains before they get wide.
packages.cost: A short kick over the rushing line finds space.

packages.name: Containment
packages.summary: Keep wide runs in front of the defense.
packages.inspiration: Contain defense and rugby edge defense.
packages.scenario: Open-field early downs, especially against repeated perimeter runs.
packages.benefits: Keeps perimeter runs in front of the defense and reduces their explosive potential.
packages.cost: Concedes inside runs.

packages.name: Robber Coverage
packages.summary: Take away the middle depth kick pass.
packages.inspiration: Intermediate zone robber concepts.
packages.scenario: Late downs and frequent territory releases.
packages.benefits: Closes the intermediate kick-pass lane.
packages.cost: Concedes deep bombs and interior runs.
packages.counter: Throw over the robber or run inside.

packages.name: Lateral Trap
packages.summary: Invite the first lateral and contest the next.
packages.inspiration: Rugby and lacrosse second-phase pressure.
packages.scenario: Early downs, especially when the opponent repeatedly laterals.
packages.benefits: Invites the first lateral but contests later transfers more aggressively.
packages.cost: Concedes straight inside runs and quick kick passes.
packages.counter: Avoid chaining laterals into the trap.

packages.name: Exhaustion Press
packages.summary: Send extra rushers to hurry short kick passes.
packages.inspiration: Pressing a fatigued opponent.
packages.scenario: Early in a series against tired on-field offensive personnel.
packages.benefits: Commits extra rushers and disrupts short releases.
packages.cost: Costs defender energy and exposes space behind the rush.
packages.counter: A protected long kick or fresh interior runners.

packages.name: Anchor Crease
packages.summary: Use inside leverage to keep a short power drive moving.
packages.inspiration: gridiron/rugby
packages.scenario: inside leverage
packages.benefits: inside leverage
packages.cost: limited perimeter threat

packages.name: Pod Two
packages.summary: Keep two runners close for quick, controlled lateral support.
packages.inspiration: rugby/gridiron
packages.scenario: short support chain
packages.benefits: short support chain
packages.cost: transfer exposure

packages.name: Edge Three
packages.summary: Use a wider chain of support runners to stretch the edge.

packages.scenario: longer perimeter chain
packages.benefits: longer perimeter chain
packages.cost: compound turnover risk

packages.name: Last Wave
packages.summary: String together wide laterals when a late deficit calls for a big gain.

packages.scenario: desperation support chain

packages.cost: extreme turnover risk
